skill.name: opentargets-database
skill.description: Query the Open Targets Platform for target-disease associations, evidence, drug data, tractability, and safety annotations.
skill.summary: Retrieve Open Targets evidence for therapeutic target discovery and drug repurposing research.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill contains intentional outbound GraphQL access to the public Open Targets API, which creates a low disclosure risk for submitted query terms. The command-execution and reconnaissance alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline identifiers, and biomedical GraphQL fields. No prompt injection, credential access, filesystem abuse, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Outbound API requests send user query terms to Open Targets.
remediation.suggestion: Document that search terms leave the local environment and warn users not to submit secrets or private patient data.

remediation.issue: Repeated exploratory queries can depend heavily on the public API.
remediation.suggestion: Add caching, pagination limits, and guidance to use downloads or BigQuery for bulk analyses.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples create noisy command-execution scanner matches.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples clearly labeled as Python and avoid ambiguous inline backticks in security-sensitive metadata.

content.user_title: Query Open Targets Drug Discovery Data
content.value_statement: Drug discovery teams need structured evidence before selecting therapeutic targets. This skill queries Open Targets data and explains associations, evidence, drugs, and risks.
actual_capabilities: Search Open Targets for targets, diseases, and drugs by name or identifier.
Retrieve target annotations, including tractability, safety liabilities, genetic constraint, and associated diseases.
Fetch disease profiles with therapeutic areas, associated targets, and known drugs.
Retrieve evidence records for a target-disease pair and filter by evidence type.
Summarize known drugs, mechanisms, targets, clinical phases, and indication status.
Provide GraphQL endpoint guidance and interpretation notes for Open Targets scores.
limitations: Requires internet access to the public Open Targets API.
Not designed for bulk systematic analyses across many entities.
Association scores are rankings, not clinical success probabilities.
Does not replace primary literature review or expert biomedical validation.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Disease Targets
use_cases.description: Find disease-associated genes, compare evidence types, and shortlist targets for deeper review.

use_cases.title: Assess Target Readiness
use_cases.description: Review tractability, safety liabilities, genetic constraint, and clinical precedence for one gene.

use_cases.title: Explore Drug Repurposing
use_cases.description: Identify known drugs for a disease and compare mechanisms, targets, and clinical phases.

prompt_templates.title: Find an Entity
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search for one target, disease, or drug.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Open Targets for "BRCA1" as a target. Return the best identifier, name, entity type, and short description.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Target
prompt_templates.scenario: Target assessment after an Ensembl identifier is known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess ENSG00000157764 in Open Targets. Summarize tractability, safety liabilities, genetic constraint, and the strongest disease associations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Evidence Types
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of a target-disease hypothesis.
prompt_templates.prompt: For ENSG00000157764 and EFO_0000249, retrieve evidence by data type. Explain which evidence is strongest and which needs manual review.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a Disease Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for target discovery planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: For Alzheimer disease, identify top associated targets, compare evidence, flag safety or tractability concerns, and recommend three targets for follow-up.

output_examples.input: Assess BRAF as a therapeutic target.
output_examples.output: The skill returns the Ensembl identifier, target name, tractability signals, safety notes, top disease links, and evidence categories to review.

output_examples.input: Find known drugs for Alzheimer disease.
output_examples.output: The skill summarizes drug names, target genes, mechanisms, clinical phases, indication status, and caveats for repurposing decisions.

output_examples.input: Compare evidence for one target-disease pair.
output_examples.output: The skill groups evidence by genetics, known drugs, pathways, expression, animal models, and literature, then explains confidence limits.

best_practices: Start with exact Open Targets identifiers before comparing evidence.
Review evidence type breakdowns instead of relying only on the overall score.
Use downloads or BigQuery for large studies instead of repeated API calls.
anti_patterns: Treating Open Targets scores as clinical success probabilities.
Using text-mining evidence alone for target prioritization.
Submitting private patient data or confidential project details to the public API.

faq.question: Does this skill require authentication?
faq.answer: No. The Open Targets GraphQL API is public and does not require an API key.

faq.question: Can it run large systematic studies?
faq.answer: It is best for exploratory queries. Use Open Targets downloads or BigQuery for large analyses.

faq.question: What identifiers does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Ensembl gene IDs for targets, EFO IDs for diseases, and ChEMBL IDs for drugs.

faq.question: Are association scores confidence scores?
faq.answer: No. They rank relative evidence strength and require biological and clinical interpretation.

faq.question: Can it assess drug safety?
faq.answer: It can retrieve safety liabilities, expression, constraint, and withdrawn drug information for review.

faq.question: Does it replace expert validation?
faq.answer: No. It supports evidence gathering, but primary literature review and expert validation remain necessary.
